definition.description: From a supported hands-and-knees position, set both knees comfortably wide with lower legs supported. Rock the hips posteriorly through a comfortable range, then return under control. One repetition is one rock-back and return. This excludes a unilateral straight-leg Adductor Rockback, static frog position, lateral lunge, Cossack shift, Copenhagen exercise, crawl, assessment, and forced end range.

environment.space: room to enter and exit a wide-kneeling hands-supported base
environment.changeRule: Changing knee width, lower-leg position, hand height, range, tempo, pause, load, surface, dose, or intent requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: can use the assigned floor or elevated-hand base
clear stable surface and exit path
can perform a small comfortable rock-back without symptom escalation
understands the stop signal and session logistics fit
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, unsafe base, surface, support, or communication conflict
sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal knee width, foot orientation, range, dose, recovery, outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 59 reassessed against the Adductor Rockback family boundary; the bilateral bent-knee frog base is a distinct definition.

anatomy.laterality: bilateral symmetrical lower-limb base; record any deliberate side shift separately
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics only; no diagnosis, treatment, flexibility, injury-prevention, or performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate low-load wide-kneeling hip-access work only when the exact base, support, range, and dose fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Set a comfortable wide-knee base, rock back gently, then return before you force range or round your back.
secondaryCues: use the assigned mat, padding, or hand height
make the range or width smaller before forcing depth
stop before pinching, pain, or passive sinking
expectedSensations: light trunk and upper-limb support effort
unexpectedSensations: pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, unsafe support, or a range that cannot be controlled
selfChecks: knees and lower legs stay in the assigned base

observationChecklist: exact bilateral frog base, knee width, lower-leg and hand-support variant
range, cadence, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.forced_width_or_range: narrow the knees or range, elevate the hands, or stop
faultCorrections.lumbar_rounding_or_passive_sink: reduce range and restore an active controlled return
faultCorrections.support_discomfort: add padding or use another reviewed task after revalidation

doNotUseWhen: the floor, support, exit route, or communication is unsafe
the task conflicts with symptoms or restrictions
the intended task is unilateral adductor rocking, a static frog hold, standing lateral movement, adductor strengthening, crawling, assessment, or forced range

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved safety, symptom, base, support, or quality issues.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any task change reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, and validation.

sourceVariant.archiveReason: The source lacks an exact rock-return cycle, comfortable width/support/range contract, fatigue tracking, delivery profiles, alternate boundaries, calibration, and review gates.

requirements.cycleRule: one controlled posterior hip rock-back and return is one repetition
requirements.rangeRule: comfortable range without forced knee width, pinching, passive sinking, or trunk compensation

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate low-dose bilateral wide-kneeling hip-access preparation.

dosage.countRule: count only controlled rock-back returns completed at the assigned base without forced range or compensation

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The assigned bilateral frog base and support remain stable, the rock-back and return are controlled, the trunk remains organised, range is comfortable, and no stop symptom appears.
stopRules: stop on pain, new symptoms, dizziness, unsafe support, or participant request
stop when knee width, range, trunk, upper-limb support, or exit control cannot be restored
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Assign knee width, foot/lower-leg position, hand height, and range; observe from front and side; reduce width or range before adding volume; revalidate any alternate.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Set the assigned wide-knee base, breathe, gently rock hips back, return under control, and stop before you force range or lose support.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate preparation only; no outcome is guaranteed.

doseScaling.reduce: narrower knee width, shorter range, slower cadence, elevated hands, padding, more rest, or another reviewed task
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not force width or depth, add load, turn the task into a static sink, or substitute a unilateral/standing/strength task without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Comfortable width, gentle rock, controlled return.
supportPrompts.coach: Wide-knee frog is an exact base, not an athlete-skill label.

legacy.description: Archived Source 59 remains traceable as an underspecified wide-knee rockback skeleton.
legacy.loadNote: Candidate-only; use the exact wide-kneeling base and record range, knee width, support, compensation, and symptoms.
legacy.cardSummary: Source 59 is represented by an exact candidate contract rather than its vague legacy row.
legacy.coachLanguage: Use an exact candidate only after base, range, support, duration, fatigue, and downstream-demand checks.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Comfortable wide knees; gently rock and return.

coachingExecution.quality_gate: Legacy source is not selectable; use exact candidate contract.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact base, knee width, hand support, range, controlled rock-return, symptoms, communication, dose, and downstream task—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: confirm assigned floor, mat, knee width, hand support, and exit route
confirm a small controlled rock-back and return
confirm stop signal and clear path
stopSigns: dizziness, chest, neurologic, circulation, balance, or support symptoms
unsafe surface, forced range, passive sinking, or persistent quality loss
contraindications: unilateral adductor-rockback, static frog-hold, lateral-lunge, adductor-strength, crawl, assessment, or forced-range intent
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after revalidation.
Do not treat unilateral Adductor Rockback, static Frog Stretch, lateral lunge/Cossack, Copenhagen work, or crawling as automatic substitutions.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment; independent calibration required.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact bilateral wide-kneeling Frog Rockback only.
